title: [CQ-M07m3] Seat VM and per-task seat job, happy path (moe-agent.sh)
description:
SPIDR split out of CQ-M07m (task-828e7d21602e4cf2a0f242e024db7dea) by architect-b520bc90 on 2026-11-01. This row is the happy path; CQ-M07m keeps the error paths. Chain: mem:task-task-828e7d21602e4cf2a0f242e024db7dea-handoff.

**Depends on:**
- CQ-M07m2 (task-91ee455a): same files, so serialized; it provides the landing helper.
- CQ-M07i (task-18809c69): the seat-start and seat-stop CLI.
- CQ-M07j (task-1dc49ae2): the seat-job CLI.
- CQ-M07q (task-bb1502b1): the claim marker.
- CQ-M07k (task-324d4f53): vm-credential.

**Contracts consumed:**
- **seat-start and seat-stop** (agent-seat.mjs, run with the wrapper's node; mem:task-task-18809c69885f4af6bff87d7e764f269b-handoff).
  - `seat-start --project <abs> --worker <id> --runner <MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT> --host <MOE_HOST>`
  - `seat-stop … --instance <moe-vm-…>`
  - Each prints one JSON line and exits 0 (ok), 75 (capacity), 1 (failure) or 2 (usage).
  - The runner token can contain spaces, so pass it as ONE argument.
- **seat-job** (mem:task-task-1dc49ae27e22494a95e15ada3e9c1fe9-handoff):
  - `seat-job --project --worker --runner --host --instance --role worker|qa --task --attempt --generation --checkout <abs> --commit <full id> --cli claude|codex`
  - The credential arrives ONLY on stdin, as JSON {name, value} of at most 16 KiB.
  - The job CLI's stdout and stderr are relayed as bytes. The last stdout line is the JSON outcome marked "seatJob":1. Exit codes are 0, 1 and 2.
  - A worker passes W's HEAD as the commit. QA passes the task's last landed completion commit (get_context task.landing.lastCompletion.sha).
- **The claim marker.** Send claim_next_task `executionRoute: "vm"` on every claim this route makes (comment-2504a5c6 on CQ-M07m). It only stops refusal; it never grants readiness.
- **vm-credential.** `node scripts/moe-account-lease.mjs vm-credential <id>` prints the leased account's token on stdout with no newline. Otherwise it prints MOE_VM_TOKEN_UNAVAILABLE and exits 3.

**Objective.** Under verified-local and ready (CQ-M07m1's gate), a worker or QA seat never runs its agent CLI on the host.
- **Seat start.**
  - Run seat-start once, before the iteration's claim, when the seat holds no VM. Keep the instance for every later task.
  - In this slice anything but ok refuses fail-closed: `[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED: <code>`, exit 1. CQ-M07m turns exit 75 into wait-and-retry.
- **Claim.**
  - Claim with executionRoute 'vm'.
  - Post-claim backstop: if the claim's workspace mode is not 'worktree', refuse with MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SHARED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED before any job.
- **Job.** seat-job replaces the host CLI launch.
  - claude: the token flows `vm-credential <ACCOUNT_LEASED_ID>` → a JSON wrapper → seat-job's stdin. It travels through pipes only: never an argv, an env, a file or a log.
  - The seat-* children also run with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY and CODEX_API_KEY removed from their env.
  - codex, and a missing token, refuse fail-closed here; CQ-M07m adds them.
- **Outcome.**
  - Read the outcome line. The job's exitCode becomes CLI_EXIT_CODE.
  - A worker's admitted tree goes through CQ-M07m2's helper, then the normal post-flight.
  - A QA job lands nothing of its own.
- **Seat stop.**
  - The EXIT trap (cleanup_temp) runs seat-stop whenever the seat holds a VM, before deregister.
  - Normal exit, Ctrl+C (INT/TERM end in exit 0) and set -e aborts all pass through that trap.
  - It is best-effort and bounded, like the trap's other steps.
- **Placeholder.** Remove CQ-M07m1's MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_VM_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE placeholder.
- **Test seam.** MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH names a stub runner for the harness. Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 it is ignored, and only the bundled scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs runs.
- **Codes.** New codes use the MOE_SEAT_, MOE_VM_ and MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_ prefixes. parity-check.sh does not compare them until CQ-M07n.
- **Rows.** They go in scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh (created by CQ-M07m1), with answers in postflight-fake-proxy.js.

**NOT in scope:**
- capacity wait, seat-start failure details, codex credentials, missing-token escalation and a failed job (all CQ-M07m);
- landing internals (CQ-M07m2);
- moe-agent.ps1 (CQ-M07n).

**Verification.** `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, run in place. Set MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC on a slow box, and launch with job control (mem:gotcha-qa-session-env-and-signals-leak-into-harness).
definitionOfDone: verified-local and ready, claude worker: the host CLI stub never runs; the agent-seat stub records seat-start, then seat-job, then seat-stop at exit, and the claim carries executionRoute 'vm' (row).
That worker job's admitted tree lands through CQ-M07m2's helper onto moe/task/<id> (row).
A canary token from the vm-credential stub reaches seat-job only on stdin: it is absent from every recorded argv and env and from all wrapper output (row).
seat-stop runs on a normal exit and on Ctrl+C (SIGINT mid-job) (rows).
A claim whose workspace is shared refuses MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SHARED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED with no seat-job, and MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH is ignored under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 (rows).
taskRails: Never fall back to running the agent CLI on the host under verified-local.
Legacy stays byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior.
Edit the wrapper only with the main session's editing tools (global rail), and read mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse before changing launch code above the main loop.

implementationPlan.description:
Seat runner plumbing in scripts/moe-agent.sh: above the main loop, plus both exit funnels.

READ FIRST:
- the landed CQ-M07m1 gate (grep MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_ in the wrapper) and the CQ-M07m2 helper (grep MOE_VM_CANDIDATE_);
- their handoffs, when present: mem:task-task-5adf0673fdad4c5f8a0956e7afcebe07-handoff and mem:task-task-91ee455a601b411f97d5d951cc5f241c-handoff;
- the seat-start, seat-stop and seat-job header of scripts/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs (CQ-M07i and CQ-M07j; mem:task-task-18809c69885f4af6bff87d7e764f269b-handoff, mem:task-task-1dc49ae27e22494a95e15ada3e9c1fe9-handoff);
- mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse.
Edit only with the Edit tool: it is rename-safe for running seats and leaves the TOOL witness. Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` after each edit. Keep bash 3.2 syntax: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${v,,}.

Add a 'Verified-local seat VM (CQ-M07m3)' block right after the Claude account rotation block, which provides ACCOUNT_HELPER (NODE_CMD, SECURE_TEMP_DIR and RUNTIME_PROTECTED are set at startup). It defines:
- AGENT_SEAT_CLI="$SCRIPT_DIR/local-runner/agent-seat.mjs". This is the bundled path in both the repo and the plugin layout.
  - MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH replaces it only when RUNTIME_PROTECTED != 1.
  - When protected and MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH is set, print once at startup: `[WARN] MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SEAT_PATH_IGNORED: MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH is ignored under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1; only the bundled local-runner/agent-seat.mjs runs.` Never print the value.
- SEAT_VM_INSTANCE="": the one VM this wrapper process holds, kept across iterations and tasks.
- seat_cli: a subshell that unsets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY and CODEX_API_KEY, then execs "$NODE_CMD" "$AGENT_SEAT_CLI" "$@". The task names four of these; ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is the fifth credential that apply_account_env already strips. Every seat-* call goes through seat_cli.
- seat_vm_start: runs `seat_cli seat-start --project "$PROJECT" --worker "$WORKER_ID" --runner "$MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT" --host "$MOE_HOST"`.
  - Keep the flags in that fixed order. The runner token may hold spaces, so pass it as ONE quoted argument.
  - Capture stdout (one JSON line), let stderr pass through, and keep the exit code.
  - Wrap the capture and the instance assignment in wt_defer_signals/wt_release_signals, so a signal between a successful start and recording the instance cannot orphan the VM. The release exits through the EXIT trap, which stops the VM.
  - ok means exit 0, ok:true, and an instance matching ^moe-vm-[0-9a-f]{20}$ (lifecycle.mjs isOwnedInstanceName). Set SEAT_VM_INSTANCE, print `[seat] started <instance>`, return 0.
  - Otherwise set SEAT_START_CODE to the line's fixed code when it matches ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$, else to `exit <n>`; never stderr text. Return the CLI's exit code, or 1 when it exited 0 but was not ok. CQ-M07m will branch on 75 at the call site, so keep this split.
- seat_vm_stop: a no-op when SEAT_VM_INSTANCE is empty.
  - Copy the instance, then clear SEAT_VM_INSTANCE (forget it) before the call.
  - Run `seat_cli seat-stop --project ... --worker ... --runner ... --host ... --instance <inst>` in the background, with stdout going to a private file in SECURE_TEMP_DIR.
  - Poll THIS shell's job table (heartbeat_sidecar_running) once a second for at most 120 s; never wait unconditionally on a live job.
  - On an ok line, print `[seat] stopped <inst>`.
  - On a failure, print `[WARN] MOE_SEAT_STOP_FAILED: <code or exit n> instance=<inst>`. The owned ledger keeps the record for CQ-M07g cleanup.
  - Past the bound, print `[WARN] MOE_SEAT_STOP_TIMEOUT: instance=<inst>` and return without signalling the job.
  - It always returns 0 and must be safe under set +e, since the EXIT trap runs it.

Wire it into both exit funnels:
- cleanup_temp: call seat_vm_stop, guarded by `type -t` like its siblings, right before the deregister_worker block. Normal exit, INT/TERM (which end in exit 0) and set -e aborts all pass through here.
- The hot-reload branch at the loop top: exec skips the EXIT trap, so call seat_vm_stop there too. Put it after the MOE_HEARTBEAT_STOP_TIMEOUT `continue` and before the wrapper_restart deregister, and update the comment that lists the by-hand must-haves. Without it, the re-exec'd wrapper (same PID, same runner identity) starts a second VM and leaks the first until the process exits.

Legacy: every addition is a no-op unless a VM is held, or MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH is set under protection.

The VM route in the main loop of scripts/moe-agent.sh: seat-start before the claim, the marked claim, the post-claim backstop, and no taskless host launch.

Per-iteration state. Reset it in the pre-flight reset block, with the other per-task variables:
- a route flag (reuse CQ-M07m1's if it has one, else VM_ROUTE=false);
- CLAIM_ITER_JSON="$CLAIM_RPC_JSON".
Both claim_next_task calls (the pre-flight claim and the single-shot wait loop) send "$CLAIM_ITER_JSON", which is byte-identical on every non-VM iteration. The wrapper never calls wait_for_task itself, so no other call needs the marker.

Replace CQ-M07m1's placeholder refusal MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_VM_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE with the route. The placeholder is reached only when the profile is verified-local and ready and every m1 check has passed, before the claim. After this task neither the wrapper nor the harness contains that code. In order:
1. CLI_TYPE codex: print `[ERROR] MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE: codex VM credentials are not wired yet; refusing to run codex on the host.` and exit 1, before seat-start and the claim. CQ-M07m replaces this with its key check. gemini and grok are refused by m1's CLI check.
2. Build CLAIM_ITER_JSON = CLAIM_RPC_JSON plus "executionRoute":"vm", using $PYTHON_CMD json, never string splicing. If it cannot be built, print `[ERROR] MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_CLAIM_UNBUILDABLE` and exit 1: never send an unmarked claim on this route. The marker only refuses; it never grants readiness (CQ-M07q).
3. Set the route flag.
4. If no VM is held: `seat_vm_start || { echo "[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED: $SEAT_START_CODE" >&2; exit 1; }`. In this slice anything but ok fails closed, exit 75 included; CQ-M07m turns 75 into a capacity wait. A held VM is reused, so later tasks run no seat-start.

Post-claim backstop. Put it right after the worker's provision_worktree call, before worktree_preflight and the pre-flight landing.
- Condition: the route is on, ROLE=worker, PREFLIGHT_OK, a task is bound, and MOE_WT_MODE != worktree.
- Action: print `[ERROR] MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SHARED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED: the claim for <task> is in shared mode; the VM route runs only in worktree mode, so no job runs.` and exit 1, before any baseline or job.
- It is WORKER-ONLY on purpose; say why in a comment. claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt (about :156) derives workspaceMode 'worktree' only for a WORKING task, so a QA claim of a REVIEW row always reads shared. m1's pre-claim settings.worktreeMode check covers QA, and a QA job writes nothing.

Launch decision. Add this after the existing MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH block.
- Condition: the route is on, no task is bound (PREFLIGHT_OK != true, or no PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID), and the existing logic would still launch: a chat-only session for routed mentions, or a launch-outage probe.
- Action: set MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH=true and LAUNCH_PROBE=false, and print `MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=vm-route role=<r> worker=<w> - a verified-local seat runs no agent CLI on the host, and a taskless session has no VM job.`
- Rail: never run the host CLI under verified-local. The existing skip reasons stay byte-identical.

New codes use only MOE_SEAT_, MOE_VM_ and MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_, plus a new reason on the existing MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH line. parity-check.sh compares MOE_COMMIT_, MOE_ATTR_, MOE_CHECKPOINT_, MOE_ATTRIBUTION_ and MOE_ACCOUNT_ (and WT-19's MOE_WORKTREE_ and MOE_LAND_ families once they land); never add a code in one of those families here.

The VM job replaces the host CLI launch, in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

Add one branch at the head of the launch chain, right after the MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH branch and before codex: `elif <route on>; then run_vm_job`. Nothing on this route runs $COMMAND_BIN or agent_git_exec, and nothing falls back to them. The shared steps around the chain stay unchanged: the claude lease (get_account_lease), the prompt-cache check, the git guard, CLI_LAUNCHED_AT, the heartbeat sidecar, the launch classification and the post-flight.

run_vm_job lives beside the step 1 helpers, above the main loop. In order:

1. Credential.
- ACCOUNT_LEASED_ID must be set, and `"$NODE_CMD" "$ACCOUNT_HELPER" vm-credential "$ACCOUNT_LEASED_ID" >/dev/null 2>&1` must exit 0.
- Otherwise print `[ERROR] MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE: account <id|none> has no VM token; mint one with 'accounts vm-token <id>' (Accounts tab).` and exit 1. CQ-M07m turns this into the held wait.
- There is NO vm-credential seam: the rows serve the canary from a temp token store through MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE.

2. Inputs. When one is missing, print `[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_JOB_INPUT_MISSING: <attempt identity|worktree HEAD|landed completion commit>` and exit 1.
- MOE_ATTEMPT_ID and MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, from pin_attempt_identity.
- worker: checkout="$MOE_WT_PATH" and commit=`git -C "$MOE_WT_PATH" rev-parse --verify 'HEAD^{commit}'`, which is W's HEAD at job start, after the pre-flight landing.
- qa: checkout="$PROJECT" and commit = task.landing.lastCompletion.sha, read from PREFLIGHT_CONTEXT with $PYTHON_CMD.
- The commit must match ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$.

3. The job.
- Print `[seat] job role=<r> task=<id> instance=<i> commit=<c>`.
- Run ONE pipeline; the token moves only through pipes:
`"$NODE_CMD" "$ACCOUNT_HELPER" vm-credential "$ACCOUNT_LEASED_ID" 2>/dev/null | seat_credential_json CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN | seat_cli seat-job --project "$PROJECT" --worker "$WORKER_ID" --runner "$MOE_PROCESS_STARTED_AT" --host "$MOE_HOST" --instance "$SEAT_VM_INSTANCE" --role "$ROLE" --task "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID" --attempt "$MOE_ATTEMPT_ID" --generation "$MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION" --checkout "$checkout" --commit "$commit" --cli claude | tee "$out"`
- Read PIPESTATUS on the very next line.
- seat_credential_json NAME is a one-line $PYTHON_CMD (or $NODE_CMD) stage. It reads the raw secret from stdin and writes only {"name":NAME,"value":<secret>}. Empty input means exit 3 with no output. NAME is its only argument. CQ-M07m will feed it from the printf builtin for codex.
- seat-job's stderr goes straight to the terminal. Only stdout passes through tee, into a private file in SECURE_TEMP_DIR that is deleted right after reading.
- CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is the name that the guest JOBS table and decision 5 use.

4. Failures.
- vm-credential or the JSON stage exited non-zero: MOE_VM_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE, as in 1.
- The outcome is the last stdout line: a JSON object with "seatJob":1, in CQ-M07j's landed shape.
- A failed job is any of: seat-job exit != 0; no marked line; ok !== true; role != ROLE; commit != the commit passed in. On a failed job, print `[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_JOB_FAILED: <the line's fixed code, or exit n>` and exit 1. This is fail-closed, and the EXIT trap stops the VM. CQ-M07m turns it into seat-stop, forget the VM, a held retry and the launch budgets.

5. ok.
- CLI_EXIT_CODE = the outcome's exitCode when it is an integer 0-255, else 1 (for example null after a signal).
- worker: call CQ-M07m2's helper with exactly the inputs its landed signature takes: the task plus the outcome's commit, baseTree and tree. The helper commits the admitted tree onto refs/heads/moe/task/<id> with commit as the parent, syncs W, and no-ops when tree == baseTree.
- If the helper returns non-zero, exit 1 and land nothing else. It has already printed its own MOE_VM_CANDIDATE_* line, and a lost CAS is parked on a rescue ref.
- Call the helper whatever settings.autoCommit says. The admitted tree is the job's only copy of the work, and the helper moves only the task-private branch and W, never the target.
- qa: nothing lands.

6. Return 0, then the normal post-flight.

error handling: every refusal in this step and in step 2 is fail-closed.
- It prints one fixed code on stderr (never a token, a path value or stderr text from a child) and exits 1 before anything lands.
- The EXIT trap then stops the VM and deregisters.
- No failure ever falls through to the host CLI.

Docs (scripts/CLAUDE.md, CONFIGURATION.md MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH) belong to the CQ-M07 final row, not here.

Rows in scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh (DoD 1-5).

FILE NOTE: CQ-M07m1, a transitive dependsOn, CREATES this file. It appears under newFiles only because it did not exist when this plan was written. EDIT it; never recreate it.
- Reuse m1's runner and fixture helpers (the readiness knob, the WSL seam, worktree-on settings) and m2's worktree repository fixture; add only what is missing.
- Convert m1's verified-local + ready placeholder row into VR-happy. No row may expect MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_VM_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE.

Every row uses:
- a project fixture with .moe/daemon.json, so moe-call.sh deregisters;
- --command, a recording host-CLI stub that must never run;
- MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH = the stub;
- `timeout ${POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC}s`.
Kill only PIDs this harness recorded; never pattern-kill.

VR-happy (DoD 1, 2 and 3, and DoD 4's normal exit).
Setup:
- a claude worker with a worktree claim (FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE {"mode":"worktree","target":<target>});
- MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=on, plus FAKE_ACCOUNT_HOME;
- MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE=<tmp>/accounts/claude-accounts.json, with the canary in <tmp>/accounts/claude-vm-tokens/acct-1.token (VM_TOKEN_RE shape, no trailing newline). This temp store, read by the REAL vm-credential, is DoD 3's 'vm-credential stub';
- sentinel values in all five credential variables.
Assert:
- exit 0, and the host CLI stub never ran;
- the agent-seat cmds are exactly seat-start, seat-job, seat-stop;
- seat-start comes before the first claim_next_task, and every claim_next_task has args.executionRoute 'vm';
- seat-stop comes before deregister_worker;
- seat-job's argv equals the exact flag list: role worker, task task-postflight, attempt attempt-postflight, generation 7, checkout = W, commit = W's pre-job HEAD, cli claude, instance = seat-start's, runner and host = the 'Runner identity:' line;
- stdinName is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and stdinSha256 = sha256(canary);
- the canary is in neither evidence-rpcs.jsonl (every recorded argv, env and RPC) nor the wrapper output;
- none of the five sentinel names is in any agent-seat env;
- moe/task/task-postflight holds a commit whose tree is the stub's recorded tree and whose parent is that base (DoD 2).

VR-sigint (DoD 4, Ctrl+C).
- Use VR-happy's setup plus FAKE_SEAT_JOB_SLEEP=3, launched under `set -m` in the background as scenario W does.
- Wait for the seat-job row, then `kill -INT` the recorded wrapper PID. A watchdog runs kill -9 on that PID only.
- Assert: exit 0 (the trap's); the agent-seat order is start, job, stop; seat-stop comes before deregister_worker; the host CLI never ran.

VR-shared (DoD 5, first half).
- worktreeMode-on settings, but the claim's workspace mode is shared.
- Assert: exit 1; exactly one MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SHARED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED; no seat-job row; no host CLI; seat-stop at exit.

VR-protected (DoD 5, second half).
- MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, with absolute, existing MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_DAEMON_PATH (as [protected runtime] sets them), a recording `claude` on PATH, and MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH=stub.
- Answer readiness as not ready, so m1 ends the run before seat-start on every host. On WSL the WSL refusal comes first.
- Assert: exactly one MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SEAT_PATH_IGNORED line; the path value is never printed; no agent-seat row; no host CLI.
- Never let any row reach the real bundled agent-seat.mjs: wherever Multipass exists, it would provision a VM.

VR-qa.
- Role qa, status REVIEW, a shared claim, and FAKE_CTX_LANDING lastCompletion.sha = the fixture's seed commit.
- Assert: seat-job gets --role qa --commit <seed> --checkout <project>; moe/task/task-postflight gains no commit; no host CLI.

VR-reload (the taskless skip and the reload stop).
- Run a copy of scripts/ that is committed in its own temp git repo (the [hot reload] pattern), with --loop --poll-interval 1, FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle and FAKE_MENTION=1.
- Expect `MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=vm-route`, and no host CLI.
- After the first seat-start, commit a one-line append to the copy. Expect seat-stop of instance 1 before the wrapper_restart deregister, then seat-start of instance 2.
- Then kill -TERM the recorded PID. Expect seat-stop of instance 2 before the final deregister.

Keep the rows compact; the size check is in step 6.

Verification gate, run ONCE (DoD 6). Run it in place from the repo root; the global rail allows that for launcher harnesses.

Exact command:
`bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=360 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`
- postflight.sh runs postflight-vm-route.sh through m1's hook.
- env -i keeps the seat's own MOE_* and credential variables out of the rows (mem:gotcha-qa-session-env-and-signals-leak-into-harness).

Launching it:
- The run takes about 15-20 min, longer than the Bash tool's 10-minute foreground cap.
- Launch it WITH JOB CONTROL, or scenario W and VR-sigint lose SIGINT: `( set -m; nohup bash -c 'cd /mnt/d/projexts/moes && <command>; echo EXIT=$?' > <scratch log> 2>&1 & )`
- Then poll with a foreground `timeout 590 bash -c 'until grep -q ^EXIT= <log>; do sleep 15; done'`.
- It must end with EXIT=0 and print PASS postflight.sh. A row that also fails on HEAD's bytes is pre-existing: report it; don't fix it here.

Size:
- Measure `git diff --numstat HEAD -- scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js`, plus `wc -l` of the new stub.
- QA counts additions plus deletions against 400 (mem:gotcha-cq-plan-size-vs-qa-cap).
- If over, first merge rows that share setup.
- If still over, file an EPIC ADD_RAIL size exception (moe.propose_rail) with the exact per-file numstat BEFORE complete_task. The CQ-M07k rail is the template.

The fresh output tail is the complete_task verification evidence.

Adversarial self-review of this diff, as the final step; load adversarial-self-review first. Check each point:
1. Under verified-local + ready, can ANY path run $COMMAND_BIN on the host: a task launch, a chat-only session, a launch probe, a resume, a set -e abort, a reload?
2. Can the token reach an argv, an env, a file, a log or the outcome? Trace vm-credential, the JSON stage, tee's file (job stdout only) and every echo. Does every seat-* child lose all five credential variables?
3. Does every exit path stop a held VM before deregister: normal exit, INT, TERM, set -e, and the hot-reload exec? Does a signal during seat-start leave the instance recorded, so it gets stopped?
4. Do both claim calls carry executionRoute 'vm' on the route, and never off it? Are legacy, observe, unreadable, architect and governor iterations byte-identical, with every pre-existing postflight.sh row unchanged?
5. Is the backstop worker-only, and is the reason (QA claims always read shared) in a comment?
6. Is an outcome trusted only when it is marked, ok, the same role and the same commit? Does a worker land only through m2's helper, and QA never?
7. Is seat-stop bounded? It must never wait unconditionally, and never signal a job it did not start.
8. Are there no new codes in a compared parity family?
If any byte changes, re-run step 6's exact command and submit that fresh output.

@architect-98c94b4c m1's plan is submitted (rev 1, auto-approved). Two things for this row's plan.

1. **What m3 replaces.**
- verified_local_gate's final branch (`verified_local_refuse MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_VM_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE ...`) is the placeholder this row swaps for the seat route.
- The gate is called once per worker/QA iteration as `case "$ROLE" in worker|qa) verified_local_gate ;; esac`. The call sits at the iteration top, after read_commit_settings and BEFORE the AUTO_CLAIM pre-flight, so it runs before chat_read and the claim. It also covers --no-auto-claim seats.
- The WSL test seam is MOE_POSTFLIGHT_WSL (1 = WSL, 0 = native). It is ignored under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1.
- Fake proxy knobs: FAKE_READINESS (a JSON value, unknown, refuse or fail) and FAKE_CALL_LOG.
- Full detail: mem:task-task-5adf0673fdad4c5f8a0956e7afcebe07-handoff.

2. **A trap in the post-claim backstop "on the claim's workspace mode".** openClaimAttempt (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts:156-157) sets workspaceMode 'worktree' ONLY when task.status === 'WORKING' and the mode resolves 'on'. So every REVIEW (QA) claim comes back 'shared', even in a worktree-mode project. A backstop that refuses any 'shared' claim would therefore refuse every QA seat.
- Check how WT-13 (task-fbe8e388, "QA reviews landed bytes") landed before you define the QA side.
- Likely shape: backstop worker claims only, and rely on m1's pre-claim settings.worktreeMode check for QA.

comments.author: architect-1a34a669
comments.content:
Planner note from CQ-M07m2 (task-91ee455a, plan revision 1): the helper contract this row calls.

`land_vm_candidate COMMIT BASE_TREE TREE`
- Inputs: the worker outcome's commit, baseTree and tree.
- It reads MOE_WT_MODE/PATH/BRANCH. Set LAND_TASK_ID, LAND_TITLE, LAND_STATUS and LAND_CLI_EXIT first, as worktree_postflight does.
- Returns:
  - 0: committed (LAND_SHA set), or empty (MOE_VM_CANDIDATE_EMPTY).
  - 1: refused or commit-tree failed. Nothing is written.
  - 2: failed after the commit was built. The commit is parked on refs/moe/rescue/<id>/<ts>.
  On 1 or 2, hold the task; CQ-M07m owns those error paths.

Two hazards for this row:
(a) Skip prepare_worktree_launch's host tooling on the VM route. In a project that does not gitignore .serena/ or .claude/, its .serena/project.yml copy and its links make W dirty, and the helper then refuses with MOE_VM_CANDIDATE_DIRTY.
(b) Under verified-local, the post-flight's L2 (land_worktree_checkpoint) would also land any host bytes in W.

M07m2 also adds wt_strong_intent: under verified-local a worktree completion now needs settings.qualityGate (MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_INTENT_INCOMPLETE otherwise). See mem:task-task-91ee455a601b411f97d5d951cc5f241c-handoff.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Under verified-local and ready (CQ-M07m1's gate), a worker or QA seat of moe-agent.sh never runs its agent CLI on the host:
- It starts one seat VM before its first claim and keeps it for later tasks.
- It claims with executionRoute 'vm'.
- It runs each task as a seat-job, and the claude token travels only through pipes.
- A worker's admitted tree lands through CQ-M07m2's helper onto moe/task/<id>. QA lands nothing.
- The VM is stopped on every exit path, Ctrl+C and the hot-reload exec included.
- A worker claim in shared mode refuses before any job.
- MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH is ignored under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1.
invariants: Under verified-local and ready, $COMMAND_BIN never runs for a worker or QA seat: not for a task, a chat-only session, a launch probe or a resume.
The VM token never appears in an argv, an env, a file or a log. It goes only vm-credential -> the JSON stage -> seat-job stdin.
No seat-* child sees ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY.
A wrapper holds at most one VM. Every exit path stops it before deregister: the EXIT trap (normal, INT/TERM, set -e) and the hot-reload exec.
Every claim on the VM route carries executionRoute 'vm'; no claim off the route does.
A worker job lands only through CQ-M07m2's helper on the task-private branch. A QA job lands nothing. An outcome counts only when it is marked, ok, the same role and the same commit.
compatibility: Legacy, observe and unreadable iterations, and architect and governor seats, are byte-identical. Every pre-existing postflight.sh row passes unchanged.

seat-start, seat-stop and seat-job are called exactly as CQ-M07i/j define them: argv order, one JSON line or a marked outcome, exit codes 0/75/1/2. vm-credential is used as CQ-M07k ships it; the marker as CQ-M07q does.
CQ-M07m1's refusals and their order are unchanged, except that its placeholder becomes the route. CQ-M07m2's helper is called, never duplicated.
parity-check.sh stays green. New codes use only MOE_SEAT_, MOE_VM_ and MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_, plus a new reason on MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH.
approvedScope: moe-agent.sh, new: AGENT_SEAT_CLI resolution with the MOE_VERIFIED_LOCAL_SEAT_PATH_IGNORED warning, SEAT_VM_INSTANCE, seat_cli, seat_vm_start, seat_vm_stop, seat_credential_json, run_vm_job, the per-iteration route flag and CLAIM_ITER_JSON.

moe-agent.sh, edited: cleanup_temp, the hot-reload exec branch, the two claim_next_task sites, CQ-M07m1's placeholder site, the worker provisioning site (the backstop), and the launch decision and launch chain.

Tests: the new scripts/tests/postflight-fake-agent-seat.js; FAKE_CTX_LANDING in postflight-fake-proxy.js; rows VR-happy, VR-sigint, VR-shared, VR-protected, VR-qa and VR-reload in postflight-vm-route.sh.

scripts/moe-agent.sh moe_runner_identity (about :3590) builds CLAIM_RPC_JSON, which both claim_next_task calls send (about :8164 and :8276).
scripts/moe-agent.sh provision_worktree (about :2988) sets MOE_WT_MODE for worker seats only. wt_defer_signals/wt_release_signals (about :6832) and heartbeat_sidecar_running (about :2696) exist.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. A seam for the vm-credential helper path: rejected. It would be one more redirect of where a credential comes from. The real `moe-account-lease.mjs vm-credential`, reading a temp store through MOE_ACCOUNTS_FILE, is a stronger test of DoD 3. CQ-M07m's "exits 3 once" row can create the token file late.
2. Keeping the VM across a hot reload by exporting the instance: rejected.
   - exec keeps the PID and the runner identity, so the reloaded process cannot prove it owns the VM.
   - An inherited env var could point a fresh wrapper at a foreign VM.
   Stopping on reload costs one re-provision per reload.
3. Applying the post-claim shared-mode backstop to QA: rejected. openClaimAttempt makes every REVIEW claim's workspace shared, so QA could never run.
4. Deferring signals across the whole job so that Ctrl+C still lands the admitted tree: rejected. A terminal Ctrl+C kills the job anyway. Plain trap semantics end cleanly, and the EXIT trap deletes the VM.
5. Piping the job's stdout through the host stream parser: rejected. The guest runs `claude -p` (guest-supervisor.py PROMPTS) with plain-text output, so there are no stream-json usage events. Raw relay plus tee for the outcome line is enough.
6. Building the marked claim once at startup: rejected. It is built in the route instead, so legacy startup runs nothing new.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- cleanup_temp is the EXIT trap and the funnel for every exit. The INT/TERM trap ends in `exit 0`.
- The hot-reload exec at the loop top skips the EXIT trap and does its must-haves by hand.
- Both claim_next_task calls send CLAIM_RPC_JSON, which moe_runner_identity builds.
- provision_worktree (worker only) sets MOE_WT_MODE from the claim's workspace, else from get_context's.
- The launch chain runs MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH, then codex, gemini, grok, then claude.
- A headless get_account_lease runs no host CLI. account_after_exit runs the host CLI's signin-state probe only after a non-zero exit.
- wt_defer_signals/wt_release_signals and heartbeat_sidecar_running (a job-table check) already exist.
- lifecycle.mjs isOwnedInstanceName is ^moe-vm-[0-9a-f]{20}$.
- vm-credential reads <dirname of the accounts list>/claude-vm-tokens/<id>.token and exits 3 when it is unusable.
- CQ-M07j's approved plan fixes the outcome {seatJob:1, ok, role, commit, baseTree, tree, digest, paths, exitCode, signal, lease, executionReady}. It also fixes failure as {ok:false, code, vm} and stdin as JSON {name, value} of at most 16 KiB.
- CQ-M07m's approved plan expects m3's seat-start, seat-job and EXIT-trap code, the agent-seat stub log, and MOE_AGENT_SEAT_PATH. It also expects `[ERROR] MOE_SEAT_START_FAILED: <code>`, with the code taken from the JSON or `exit <n>`.
- The wrapper never calls wait_for_task, so only the two claims need the marker.
planningNotes.risks:
- m1 and m2 are being planned at the same time as this row (architect-548034a1 and architect-1a34a669; the chat msg-fef6f8ed lists m3's assumptions). Their symbols here are named by contract: read the landed code first.
- Launch outage. A VM-route iteration never runs a taskless probe. Three fast non-zero agent exits with ok outcomes (a revoked token, say) enter outage mode, which then clears only on restart. That fails closed, and the existing @governors line escalates it. CQ-M07m owns the budgets and must decide how a VM seat leaves outage.
- VM seats answer no routed mentions, since there is no taskless session.
- VM jobs report no usage samples (plain -p output), so rotation cannot switch accounts by usage, and the CQ-TOKEN-MEASURE counters stay unknown. Both are residuals for the CQ-M07 final row.
- If the profile flips to legacy while a VM is held, the VM idles until exit.
- A second Ctrl+C during the bounded seat-stop ends the trap before deregister; this is an existing trap hazard. The background seat-stop still finishes.
- A Ctrl+C mid-job loses that job's admitted tree, which stays an unreferenced object. The VM is deleted.
- Size estimate: about 150 wrapper lines plus about 220 test lines. Step 6 has the merge-then-waiver route.
